title: access-model-transition-playbook
content:
Summary:

This working playbook describes the proposed RBAC v2 permission model, the audit log schema changes, evidence automation approach, and SIEM export mapping. The goal is to migrate from RBAC v1 (coarse role buckets + org-wide admin flags) to a principled, least-privilege, attribute-aware RBAC v2 with compatibility fallbacks for Dedicated and Private customers.

Primary goals:
- Provide least-privilege defaults for platform APIs and console actions.
- Maintain very low friction for self-serve developer workflows (fast onboarding).
- Ensure complete, queryable audit trails for compliance (SOX/ISO/PCI use cases).
- Support automated evidence generation for audits (snapshotting config + logs).
- Enable real-time SIEM export with stable field mappings.

Intended audience: security, SRE, platform engineering, product (console/hosted), privacy/compliance, solutions engineering.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a layered permission model: Resource-type permissions + Action-level verbs + Scope selectors + Attribute conditions (time, IP, MFA state).
- Implement a compatibility shim that translates RBAC v1 roles into v2 policies for a rolling migration.
- Ship audit log schema v2 alongside RBAC v2 with a phased SIEM exporter upgrade.

Section A: RBAC v2 proposal (conceptual)

Model primitives:
- Subject: user/service-account/session (includes metadata: tenant_id, account_type).
- Resource: typed resource (model, deployment, route, billing, secret, org-settings).
- Action (verb): read, write, execute, manage, attach, detach, list, impersonate.
- Scope selector: exact resource_id, resource-type, tag-based selector (e.g., env:prod), or organizational-level (org/team).
- Condition: optional boolean expression over attributes (request.ip, session.mfa, request.time, request.region).
- Policy: list of allow/deny statements combining the above.

Permission examples (non-exhaustive):
- allow: subject group engineering-service-accounts -> action: execute -> resource: deployment/* -> condition: request.mfa == true OR request.source == internal-vpc
- deny: subject group contractor -> action: manage -> resource: secret/*

Role composition guidance:
- Roles are convenience bundles of policies (not the primitive enforcement unit).
- Encourage narrow roles (e.g., model-deployer, inference-operator, billing-analyst).
- Provide managed role templates for common personas, and allow custom policy authoring for advanced users.

Attribute/claims to capture on Subject token:
- subject.id, subject.type (user/service), tenant_id, teams (list), device_trust_level, last_mfa_at, session_origin, delegated_by (if impersonation).

Section B: Permissions matrix (proposal)

Core role templates (short):
- platform-admin: full manage/* on org-settings, users, billing, dedicated capacity; requires session.mfa and IP whitelisting for production orgs.
- model-deployer: allow manage on model/* and deployment/*; no billing access; restricted to tag:team == owner-team.
- inference-operator: execute on deployment/*, list on model/*, read on logs/*; read-only for billing and org-settings.
- support-agent: read on customer resources (when impersonation/consent is given), manage on support-tickets/*; Audit: all support sessions must be logged and evidence captured.
- read-only-analyst: read/list across models, deployments, metrics; cannot view secrets or config.

Notes: templates must include recommended scope selectors and example conditions. Provide JSON examples in the implementation repo (see linked_artifacts).

Section C: Audit log schema v2 (summary)

Principles:
- Immutability: logs must be signed at ingest where possible (deterministic hash + sequence).
- Rich contextualization: every audit event must include subject claims, request context, policy decision reference, and resources affected.
- Queryability: fields normalized for common SIEM queries (user.geoid, tenant.id, action, resource.type, resource.id, result, reason).

Minimal audit event fields (flat list):
- event_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), source_service, tenant_id, subject_id, subject_type, subject_groups (comma list), subject_claims (serialized key=value pairs), action, resource_type, resource_id, resource_tags (comma list), decision (allow|deny), policy_id, policy_version, request_ip, request_user_agent, session_id, request_origin, result_status (success|failure), error_code, trace_id

Example event (text):
- event_id: 7d4f8b3a-...
- timestamp: 2026-03-02T14:22:03Z
- source_service: console-api
- tenant_id: t-12345
- subject_id: u-8765
- action: manage.deployment.update
- resource_type: deployment
- resource_id: d-9987
- decision: deny
- policy_id: rbac-v2-policy-344
- request_ip: 18.234.45.12
- session_id: s-45f23

Schema compatibility notes:
- We will map current v1 fields to v2 with an adapter; v2 will include extra fields but ensure the core timestamp/actor/action/resource triad remains consistent.

Section D: SIEM export mapping (deliverable)

Objectives:
- Provide deterministic mapping from audit-event fields -> SIEM ingestion schema (Splunk/Datadog/Elastic).
- Ensure field names are stable across minor schema bumps; use semantic versions for exporter.

Proposed mapping (examples):
- audit.event_id -> event_id
- audit.timestamp -> @timestamp
- audit.subject_id -> user.id
- audit.tenant_id -> tenant.id
- audit.action -> event.action
- audit.resource_type/resource_id -> object.type / object.id
- audit.decision -> event.outcome
- audit.policy_id -> tags.policy_id (or event.policy)

Transport considerations:
- Exporter supports batch push (HTTPS, compressed JSONL) and streaming (gRPC).
- Retry/backpressure: exporter will persist to local durable queue (leveldb) before forwarding. Backpressure triggers local retention policy and alert to SRE if queue > 1 hour.

Section E: Evidence automation (audit-ready bundles)

What an evidence bundle contains:
- Snapshot of RBAC policies in effect (policy_id + policy text + version).
- Signed audit-event slice (time range + hashes).
- Config snapshot (deployment config, network ACLs, billing tiers) relevant to events.
- Proof of signature keys and rotation history.
- Human-readable summary (timeline) and machine index for rapid lookup.

Automation flow:
1) Trigger: periodic (daily), scheduled (week-of-audit), or event-driven (e.g., escalation).
2) Gather: query audit store for time range and matching tenant/resources.
3) Collect: current policy set, effective policy versions for each decision, service configs, and relevant logs (trace ids).
4) Package: sign bundle with KMS, compute bundle manifest (hashes), store in secure bucket with retention policy and access audit.
5) Notify: create a ticket (JIRA/Confluence link) and optionally push to customer portal for Private deployments.

Security controls: minimal access to generated bundles, single-use presigned URLs, short TTL when shared externally, and full audit trail of any access.

Section F: Rollout plan (phased)

Phase 0 — Prep (2–3 weeks):
- Finalize policy templates and subject claim set.
- Implementation: RBAC v2 engine (policy decision point + policy store) merged behind feature flag.
- Add audit schema v2 support and exporter compatibility layer.
- Internal communications: docs, training for support/SEs.
- Tests: unit + property tests for policy evals, SIEM exporter integration tests.

Phase 1 — Canary (3–4 weeks):
- Enable RBAC v2 feature flag for internal teams and 2 pilot customers (non-prod orgs).
- Shadow mode: policy decisions logged but v1 enforcement still active.
- Validate audit logs, exporter mappings, and evidence bundle generation.
- Run tabletop drills for incident simulation and rollbacks.

Phase 2 — Soft-enforce (4–6 weeks):
- For selected non-sensitive orgs, apply RBAC v2 decisions with monitoring and auto-backout on high false-deny rate.
- Provide on-console prompts to support quick policy overrides with extra logging.
- Ramp SIEM exporter to send schema v2 fields (tagging with exporter version).

Phase 3 — Wide-enforce (8 weeks+):
- Gradual migration of all orgs to v2 policies with a compatibility converter for legacy roles.
- For Dedicated/Private customers, provide migration scripts and a one-click rollback for first 30 days.
- Require MFA + IP-whitelist checks for platform-admins by default.

Phase 4 — Post-migration stabilization (ongoing):
- Monitor errors, false-denies, latency impact of policy evals.
- Complete SIEM deprecation of v1 fields after 90 days overlap.
- Start cross-team reviews for continuous improvements.

Rollback/backout strategy:
- Feature flag off => instant revert to v1 enforcement.
- If issue limited to a tenant, apply per-tenant compatibility-mode hook that maps to v1 role buckets.
- Maintain an emergency override policy that requires 2-person authorization and is fully audited.

Section G: Metrics and alerting (SLOs)

Key metrics to track:
- Policy decision latency (p95, p99) — target p99 < 10ms for cached decisions.
- False-deny rate (from user reports and support overrides).
- Audit event delivery success (to SIEM) and queue lag.
- Evidence bundle generation time and success rate.
- Number of policy changes per week (for drift analysis).

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- policy_decision_p99 > 50ms for > 10 minutes => page SRE.
- SIEM exporter queue > 60 minutes => page infra on-call.
- sudden spike in deny outcomes for a single org (> 5x baseline) => open investigation.

Section H: Operational runbook snippets

Quick triage for a reported access failure:
1) Check audit store for event by trace_id or session_id.
2) Look up policy_id referenced in event; fetch policy version and effective conditions.
3) If quick fix required, create temporary policy override (time-boxed) and capture evidence bundle.
4) Engage owner: product/SE to update role templates; schedule follow-up.

On SIEM exporter failure:
- Confirm local queue retention state and attempt manual flush.
- If corrupted entries found, extract and re-encode as JSONL via repair script.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we implement deny-by-default for new resource types immediately, or roll out gradually?
- How much policy-writing UX do we build into the Console vs. exposing a policy-as-code file?
- Enforcement for service-to-service calls: token claims only vs. mTLS+claims?
- Exporter auth for customer-managed SIEM endpoints in Private deployments (proxy vs direct push).

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha P: finalize subject claim list and own POC for policy decision cache (due 2026-03-20).
- Marco C: implement adapter for RBAC v1->v2 mapping and run conversion on sample orgs (due 2026-03-27).
- Olivia R: define SIEM exporter versioning and release plan (due 2026-03-17).
- Diego S: draft evidence bundle retention and access policy for legal review (due 2026-03-24).

Appendix / quick links:
- Implementation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2-proto/pull/19
- Policy examples: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2-proto/examples
- SIEM mapping draft: CONFLUENCE-SEC-1782

Notes to self (working):
- Keep the initial templates conservative — aim to reduce help-desk noise.
- Consider a "policy-suggest" ML job that suggests tight selectors based on access patterns (future).
- Remember Dedicated customers may require signed offline bundles and vendor audit modes.

- [ ] run integration tests with Splunk/Elastic agents
- [ ] schedule customer pilot with Solutions Eng

simple_search_description: Working playbook for RBAC v2 migration: permission model, audit schema, SIEM export, evidence automation, rollout phases.
